item.title: Re: SCP Draft: The Consuming Mould
item.content:encoded:
This idea has been done quite a few times before, virus, end of the world, don't let it escape. What makes yours different? I advise you to check out SCP-1462 as it has a similar effect as yours. My critiques and final thoughts will be included in several collapsibles below.

Critiques
Critiques

The container must be completely synthetic, and must be cleared of any organic matter, aside from SCP-XXX itself, any time that the container is opened.

You should remove the comma between synthetic & and. You do not need a comma there because you have the word and there. Commas only need to be put before the word and if there is a list of three or more items or ideas. Instead format that sentence like this.

The container must be made of completely synthetic materials and must be cleared of any organic matter, aside from SCP-XXX itself, any time that the container is opened.

Lower clearances may enter, but only if accompanied by a level 3.

Level three what? Ogre?

attempted termination of any subjects.

I don't think that the foundation would use an unknown disease to kill people. They would kill by firing squad. If they really wanted to use an scp they would just use 173 or something. Why risk a containment breach on something that can be done with a lot less work.

To enter the wall, personnel must have level 2 clearance or higher.

This should just be removed entirely. When a sentence is marked out there should be something after it that actually pertains to what the crossed out sentence was saying. Rather after yours you continue to explain stuff that has nothing to do with the prior sentence.

access for personnel of level 3 clearance or above only, as to prevent any SCP-XXXX-A or SCP-XXXX-B instances from breaking out and wreaking havoc.

I would change the level clearance to level 4 if no experimentation or research is allowed as level three is just senior research personnel. Level four personnel are senior administrators tasked with keeping the foundation secure and preventing containment breaches.

Sorry for only critiquing your containment procedures but your article is rather long. Even though I couldn't give you tips on the rest I hope that this helps.

-

Final thoughts
Final Thoughts

I see this theme of virus SCPs pop up quite often. Here is a list of a few and it can be very hard to take these common themes and make it interesting. I want you to read a few of these articles that have to do with viruses and take note of what you like and dislike about each. I also want to know what you will do for a plot line. In my opinion doing a virus/fungus SCP is so overdone it's going to be hard to make yours interesting and stand out from the rest. Good news is that there is an audience for everything. Definitely reach out to more experienced writers and critiquers for their thoughts as they will be a lot more helpful than I am and can help you set an interesting plot to go with the article. I hope you do well in your creative writing endeavors and have a good day!

item.title: Re: yin and yang
item.content:encoded:
I'd suggest going back to the drawing board. I'm being a little blunt here for clarity and in hopes of saving you some frustration and wasted effort; this idea has numerous fundamental issues that make it highly unlikely to work.

The biggest issue is that "this entity is dangerous so the foundation has to do whatever it wants" and "entity primarily defined by an overwhelmingly strong power" were tropes that grew stale early in series I. Your target audience will not respond well to them, to the point that there are multiple snarky nicknames for both cliches.

A secondary problem here I think is that you've missed a major aspect of the modern Foundation's characterization: "The Foundation is cold, not cruel". That is, there's hundreds of examples of the Foundation being downright kind to entities in containment, when that is the most pragmatic way to ensure containment and cooperation. There are also plenty of examples of them reducing things to smoldering craters when that is the most practical means of containment. They prefer the former, but the latter is always an option.

Generally, I like it.

Of course I am going to critique a bit but keep in mind I like this idea and I can see potential in it.

 The Critique
unga bunga im a collapsible

The Good
Now, I personally dislike cognitohazard, as most new writers usually use it as an excuse for, "SCP-XXXX Makes you kill your family if you look at it. The poles are also a cognitohazard, it makes people around it become a cult, yet it does this over time, and that's the way it's done right. The poles being a cognitohazard is something that could tie into the SCP agent in the central narrative, as you could add points where they consider joining the poles, (If they are going to be around it). Honestly, I haven't searched around enough to find an SCP that makes people become parallel with poles and starve themselves to, so I liked the originality.

The Bad
These poles are must to have a certain range, or it could be considered a world ender for humanity, and because of that certain range, the SCP Foundation could just find what the range is and build a facility outside the range, no robots required. Besides if there was no range to the poles, and the pole started to attract everyone, nations could just destroy the facility around the pole and become cultist.

item.title: Re: Kamikaze mosquitoes
item.content:encoded:
Asked to review via IRC. Please keep in mind I am an author / reader, not an official critter.

Crit
hide

The area in which SCP-XXXX is found in the wild is guarded by a perimeter.

A perimeter as in what? I think of a chain-link fence when I read this, but that wouldn't be able to contain mosquitoes.

All personnel by the perimeter must wear hazmat suits or other equipment that fully covers one's person. Also, you reference the area in the article again so it might be useful to give it a designation such as "Research Site-XXXX" or something.

All personnel by the perimeter must wear hazmat suits or other equipment that fully covers one's person.

Weird wording here. Try "All personnel assigned to [designated area] must wear provided personal protective equipment at all times." You could then put a footnote here outlining what that equipment specifically is.

Personnel on neighboring sites from any level that must be terminated, Agents of groups hostile to the Foundation, and D-class may be used for this. Cause of death: Termination by SCP-XXXX.

This is an unneeded tidbit of info. I would just change the sentence before this to say "D-Class individuals".

Outdated Containment Procedures: If personnel survives an attack of SCP-XXXX, wounds need to be tended and an antihistamine cream must be applied to their skin. Medical staff needs to check for infections1 and remove possible foreign objects from the body. Infected personnel needs to be isolated until they have tested negative twice in succession.

The outdated ConProcs are a weird thing to have in the article. Wouldn't they just remove the outdated ones so that there's no confusion?

SCP-XXXX refers to a species of mosquito that only exists in the Ratargul Swamp Forest in Bangladesh.

Instead of "that only exists", try "whose habitat ranges across".

After several attacks, SCP-XXXX got taxonomically classified as the Aedes kamikaze.

Change "attacks" to encounters, change "got" to "was". Remove "the".

Larvae and pupae of SCP-XXXX mainly eat honeydew, nectar, and other plant juices until they become adults. Adult specimens suck blood from wildlife which includes but is not limited to; several primates, birds, and smaller lizards. Unlike normal mosquitoes, males from SCP-XXXX also suck blood.

This whole piece can be boiled down to "SCP-XXXX display behavior patterns identical to that of non-anomalous specimens, with the exception of male specimens seeking blood as a food source.

Upon smelling blood or observing humans, specimens will become excited and less predictable. This behavior has been described as if they are experiencing heavy withdrawal symptoms from addiction or as if they are going insane. This climaxes in specimens charging towards the individual (often accompanied with a battle cry), losing maneuverability due to their high speed, and crashing into their target or an object resulting in dead on impact. Specimens also show this behavior when they are about to release offspring or reach the end of their lifecycle.

Nothing much here, but you can continue this from the previous statement. For example "Upon detecting living humans or any amount of human blood, however, SCP-XXXX's behavior will deviate greatly from any known species of Culicidae."

I'm going to generalize for the addendums from here on out:

Alright, so your addendums are obviously where the meat of story is and do a good job of fleshing out SCP-XXXX to be more than just "killer mosquitoes". My biggest criticism of them is that they are intimidating. Generally, a wall of text will discourage the reader from continuing to read unless you're amazing at keeping someone's attention. I'd take a look back through your addendums and remove / revise any information provided during the logs that the reader can reasonably deduce themselves or that was already stated previously in the description and containment procedures.

Next individuals up for termination by SCP-XXXX: deathbygin and D-3607.

Guess I'd better put on my gear ;)

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
just_a_doctor,

As per the Draft Forum Policies, new authors are to get their concepts reviewed and greenlighted by two experienced reviewers on the Idea Critique Forums before posting on the Draft Critique Forums.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can give assistance in developing an idea before a draft is written. They can also assist in letting you know if something similar exists on the site already, or inform you of various clichés/pitfalls to be cautious of. These elements are more effectively addressed earlier in the writing process.

If you would like to request a draft review without greenlights, you can use the IRC Chatrooms to solicit critique.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note the thread in which you received them, or the users whom provided them.

item.title: Re: Delusional telekinetic
item.content:encoded:
Requested via IRC. Keep in mind I am not an official critter.

crit
hide

First off, pretty neat idea.

How did the anomaly come to be? I know you state it's recovered from a raid on Marshall, Carter and Dark. This GOI is known for selling anomalous objects and beings on the black market, so did they have any documents that the Foundation recovered on the anomaly?

I think your central narrative would work best if you focused on the Foundation's attempts at continuing the delusions, perhaps fruitlessly. So far, the narrative is lacking and seems like the biggest piece that needs attention currently.

In what way do the wings tie into the SCP? If it's anomalous properties and ability of flight actually come from telekinesis, then where did the wings come from and what purpose do they serve? Are they related to the telekinesis at all?

Currently, as the idea stands, it is a man with two unrelated anomalies: telekinesis and, for some reason, non-functional wings. I'd recommend fleshing this out more.

item.title: Re: First Project: "Amp and Damp"
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the crit! I figured characterization of the Foundation would come up as an issue, I was iffy on it. I'll probably cut the MTF involvement, I think it complicated things internally too much anyway. It makes sense that the idea to exploit them should come from the O-5s themselves and not some low level rando, but for them to consider that the anomaly would need to be powerful enough for it to be worth it, so it needs to be a strong ability but not unreasonably so. I'm considering making it a thermal and kinetic energy only anomaly, maybe also limited by physical contact with objects. I definitely need a better story beat to end on for the escaped twin, you're right that the tone doesn't really work, the problem there is I don't want both characters ending up in basically the exact same situation at the end, I think it's kinda boring that way. Gonna have to think on that one and rework the concept.

item.content:encoded:
I am a new Site Member, I might get things wrong, beware of this.

It just seems like it has been done before, and it's a reoccurring concept.

+ Here's the Critique
- hello I'm a collapsible, i open and close blocks

T.V. Show / Internet Stream SCPs have been made before and there is not many things that separate them or make them unique, SCP-993 is a Clown show that teaches children to murder, or SCP-2774, a sloth that when viewed has the possibility of you losing every function you once had.

Your Idea isn't much different, and that's the problem. A mind-altering affect if you view it that can kill you just sounds like another cognitohazard SCP. If an SCP forces a person to do something, it's a lot less scary than the person doing the thing himself without SCP interference. Take examples of SCP-5000, it's stated it's not a cognitohazard making the foundation kill.

Honestly, I can't really think of a way to make this a greenlight Idea and still have the same core structures, you can use the edit feature to make revisions to your SCP, and if you want me to critique it again after you edit, message me, I will gladly do so.

TL:DR: It's just to similar too other SCPs.

item.title: Never ending horror stream(Greenlight wanted)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type:SCP Article

Genre (Optional):(Other) Danger to public/horror

Page Layout (Optional):I plan on using a multi-document based format with the Item#, Class, Containment Procedures and Description being document i(one) each document after will have a specific purpose wether it be how this was discovered, to medical report or the tests done to attempt to understand the SCP

Elevator Pitch:The premise of the SCP is that there is a live broadcast on the internet that displays images with mind altering properties that have fatal effects, the anomalous aspect is that of the inability to prevent the stream from existing.

Central Narrative:I have not thought to much on its central narrative other than how it was discovered so I guess my answer here is “none”

Hook/Attention-Grabber:After writing I started realizing this is a semi-unique SCP as it is contained, inside-out/not in the normal way you would expect. As the stream can switch web addresses when tampered with, it can not be directly contained from the outside, but it is possible to prevent things from entering in to it to prevent damage to those persons and possibly the people around them.TL;DR: It can get out IF IT WANTS, but entities can not get in.

Additional Notes:This could be considered world-ending as it can cause mass murder if a large enough audience is reached (prevented through successful containment) and enough people experience homicidal thoughts. Also if anyone understands the SCP well enough and can help, identify or inspire a narrative for me that’d be great.

These people will eventually become a cult towards it because of the incredibly parallel nature of it. These people get slowly sucked away from reality and opt to be close to the poles and remain parallel to it at all times, dying. They also seem immovable and indestructible.

item.title: The Blood Prince
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: No (I want to hear other people’s opinions first before I proceed in adding or editing this article for greenlights.)

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP - XXXX, labeled as 'The Blood Prince', is a Keter Class Anomaly due to his superior capability of controlling animate or inanimate objects when his eyes turn red as blood. Should anything or anyone get caught in his line of sight, they become completely immobilized until they are either out of the line of sight of the SCP, or he willingly releases them.

SCP – XXXX is also capable of using his powers to hurt or kill the affected host by issuing the command towards the host and several internal and/or external injuries will inexplicably appear out of the ordinary. (This only occurs if he’s controlling a single host in his line of sight.)

The Blood Prince may appear as some average 10 yr. old boy. But during a thorough medical examination, it revealed that he was born Half-Human while the origin of the Other Half’s origin is unknown. But it did provide the boy a healing factor that allows him to regenerate from any injuries he sustains.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

An Incident occurred involving three elementary boys who were found dead in a nearby playground caused by the SCP’s power. Autopsy shows that all three of them were killed by internal injuries, but the causes of these inflicted injuries are unknown.

After the Incident, The Foundation came in and housed him in a standard humanoid containment unit. To ensure his powers doesn’t come at random, He’s been provided with a blindfold to cover his eyes to avoid any unintentional accidents to Foundation Personnel should they come in eye contact with him.

But despite his supernatural power as well as the events that occurred with it, He only wishes to live a normal life and return to his family rather than spend an entire life in isolation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: His Powers can work on almost anything or anyone, even SCPs are no exceptions to this. Apparently, his powers doesn’t work on dead material such as corpses, withered plants, and even soul-based beings.

item.title: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
seeking to greenlight: yes

Page Type: SCP article

Page layout: Audio log, Camera log MTF log

Elevator pitch: This SCP is a Mongolian (Khun) teenage boy that can manipulate any natural structure and has the ability to create Giant creature that varies depending on the SCP's imagination, however its consistent manifestation is a Asian dragon. This SCP can look through any animal that it know inner workings of (anatomy) like wolf, eagle, hummingbirds and involves any type of farm animals

However, it can't manifest creatures if it's not touching dirt or not surrounded by any natural habitats, is incredibly sensitive to fire, bomb involving any heavy firearm.

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

Central Narrative: After mass death and disappearance of local cattle and destruction of major mining factory in Erdenet Rhashaat in Mongolia, The Foundation dispatched a research team to try to find out what this SCP is. they found out that this SCP is known among the locals as a fairy tale, folklore making it alive since the Khun era.

After a couple of days, one of the nearby mining factories exploded killing all of the workers!

Learning what this SCP does The Foundation dispatched an MTF Theta-4 (Gardeners) to contain it. but GOC and Chaos Insurgency also found out about this SCP which causes all of them to go on a wild goosed chase and competition for this SCP.

the GOC tried to kill it while Chaos insurgency tried to use it. the foundation or this MTF team is preventing it.
They chase this SCP around until it get fed up with them and tries to kill them all! Which made The foundation and GOC team up to have it contained.

Hook/Attention: I'm basing the story on the SCP foundation motto. "Protect". I like the idea that the SCP Foundation is in constant competition to contain the anomaly so that no one can use them in for their own gain or kill it.

Note: this is my second SCP concept decided to put the other one in back burner.
